statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-53910 is a set of signed integer overflows in diff3 from GNU diffutils: readnum() in src/diff3.c accumulates line numbers read from the diff program's output without overflow checks, and the wrapped values are then used for memory allocation and loop bounds, so crafted diff output (for example from a program given with --diff-program) can cause out-of-bounds writes (https://cert.pl/en/posts/2026/07/CVE-2026-53910/, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-53910). The diffutils maintainers state, as recorded on the Debian tracker, that the worst outcome this issue can cause is a crash and that it cannot be used to escalate privileges; Debian rates it unimportant and has not fixed it in 1:3.10-4. Upstream fixed it in two commits: https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/diffutils.git/commit/?id=73ed7ce85cc78effb94daf028c9af6b4e5252e50 (checked multiply and add while reading each digit) and https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/diffutils.git/commit/?id=9ff04d5b84743e331e80b589335a52c5480d1815 (reject line numbers above LIN_MAX / 2). The DHI diffutils package carries a backport of both changes to readnum(). Checked every package published from this source in the DHI Debian repository, each verified against the index SHA256: the two published builds of diffutils 1:3.10-4, with their diffutils-dbgsym and diffutils-doc packages, on amd64 and arm64. The diff3 program in both diffutils builds, on both architectures, contains the LIN_MAX / 2 limit (0x3fffffffffffffff) that the fix adds, which is absent from the diff3 program in Debian's unpatched diffutils 1:3.10-4, and the changelog shipped in each build records the backport for CVE-2026-53910. diff, cmp and sdiff do not contain the affected code, which is part of diff3 only.
